title: Tiered rollforward and model-variant fallback policy for pinned versions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a deterministic, tiered fallback and automated rollforward policy for customer-pinned model versions across regions and model variants. Goals: keep customer traffic serving when a pinned model instance becomes unhealthy, deprecate pinned versions with clear grace periods and notifications, and provide per-customer override controls. The feature must preserve latency SLOs when possible, prefer same-architecture variants, and fall back to smaller/quantized variants only when necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic routed to fallback variant automatically when all pinned capacity in-region is unhealthy
Rollforward (automated next-compatible-version promotion) triggers only after configurable grace period and can be audited and reversed
Per-organization pin policy controls exposed in Console with opt-out for automated rollforward
Deprecation flow publishes a timestamped 'deprecation window' and notifies org admins via webhooks and email
Fallback selection respects policy priorities: region > model-variant compatibility score > cost threshold > latency SLO impact
E2E tests simulate multi-region outage and validate traffic continuity and billing correctness
Audit logs include fallback decision metadata (reason, candidate chosen, prior metrics) for each routed request
notes: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after spike demo showed gap when pinned model AZ had long GC pauses; design kickoff scheduled.

2026-02-25: Design review - agreed to use a deterministic priority list that includes region affinity, exact-variant, compatible-quantized-variant, and a last-resort hosted-compatible model. Trade-offs recorded: aggressive rollforward reduces downtime but can violate strict pin guarantees; therefore we added opt-out and a user-visible audit trail.
2026-03-02: Prototype implemented: fallback decision engine with scoring function = 0.5*compatibility + 0.3*latencyImpactScore + 0.2*costDelta. Need to tune weights with real traffic sims.

2026-03-05: Simulations run against replayed traffic (7 days prod sample). Results: tiered fallback maintained 99.6% request continuity with median latency uplift of 18ms; cost increased 7% for affected orgs during outage windows.

2026-03-08: Security review requested; risk: fallback could leak model names in audit logs for orgs with strict compartmentalization. Proposed mitigation: redact model identifiers in public logs and only include hashed IDs in cross-org telemetry.

2026-03-10: UX review (Console) - added per-org toggle, a deprecation details panel, and a timeline showing rollforward events. PM requested a short-circuit control to force immediate rollforward for rescue scenarios.

2026-03-12: Implementation in progress: engine endpoint integrated with smart router; unit tests for scoring and fallback order added. Marco opened PR 1973 and requested reviewers from runtime/scheduling and reliability teams. QA plan outlined below.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Core policy engine (scoring, deterministic ordering, audit payload) - runtime team - target 2 weeks
Phase 2: Router integration (per-request evaluation, circuit-breaker integration, KV-cache reconciliation) - target 1 week
Phase 3: Console controls and deprecation flows (UI + webhooks + emails) - target 1 week
Phase 4: Simulated chaos testing and canary rollout to beta orgs - target 2 weeks
Phase 5: Full rollout with monitoring playbook and postmortem template - target 1 week
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Automated rollforward could violate strict pin contracts for some enterprise customers. Mitigation: default to notify-only, provide per-org opt-in for automated rollforward, and include hard opt-out.

Risk: Latency regressions when falling back to quantized variants. Mitigation: scoring penalizes latency impact and we will block fallbacks if projected p95 exceeds SLA threshold unless org explicitly allows.

Risk: Billing anomalies when fallback uses more expensive variants. Mitigation: billing events tagged with fallback_reason; billing service will normalize for grace windows and provide refund automation for confirmed misrouting.
Risk: Information exposure in logs. Mitigation: redact model names in public dashboards and use hashed IDs; provide full details only to org admins via secure audit export.
qa_plan: Unit tests for scoring and deterministic ordering (edge cases: ties, missing variant metadata)
Integration tests across router <-> engine <-> billing, including simulated region loss
Chaos tests using step-causes: AZ down, model process OOM, kernel-level slowdown
Canary rollout to 5 beta customers with manual monitoring and rollback playbook
Post-deployment verification: anomaly detection alerts for traffic shifts and cost spikes
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal feature flag enabled for runtime team only
Stage 2: Gradual expansion with exponential ramping (25% -> 50% -> 100% of eligible orgs) over 7 days
Stage 3: Default enable for new pins with user-visible deprecation policy; existing pins unchanged unless org opts in
Rollback: feature flag off + automated rebind to customer-defined fallback (if present)
